column2: About a month afterward, Nahash camps against Jabesh-gilead; all its men request a covenant and promise service. The month is retained at this chapter's opening without inserting additional earlier events.
Nahash's covenant condition is removal of every right eye and disgrace upon Israel; the concrete threat and collective target are preserved without euphemism or elaboration.
The seven-day respite, messengers throughout Israel, conditional absence of a savior and plural you all remain. The final address includes Nahash's party, not merely singular Nahash.
Messengers reach Gibeah to Saul, speak into the people's ears and provoke the whole people's lifted voice and weeping; the collective reaction remains.
Propose restoring Behold at Saul's arrival. After the morning follows the selected temporal wording, then Saul asks about weeping and receives Jabesh's sons' report.
column3: The unusual after-the-morning expression is not silently changed to coming behind cattle; its time reference remains a specialist question.

column2: The Lord's Spirit leaps upon Saul as he hears, and his anger burns intensely against them; the source's pronoun is not expanded into an inferred target.
Two oxen are cut up and sent throughout Israel; the threat names Saul and Samuel, leaves its executing agents plural, and results in divine terror and a united cry.
column3: Cried out follows the selected verb rather than harmonizing to came out; terror renders ekstasis contextually without claiming a clinical state.

column2: Abiezek is the named mustering subject in Bama; six hundred thousand Israelite men and seventy thousand Judahite men are retained separately.
column3: The named figure and location are not silently recombined into a different place-name, nor are the numbers harmonized to another textual witness.

column2: A singular speaker sends the messengers with tomorrow's deliverance at the sun's heat; arrival, announcement and joy follow. The speaker is not explicitly renamed in this unit.

Propose you all in the first plural address, matching verse 3's distinction from the named individual Nahash. The promised coming out and invitation to do what is good before the addressed group remain.
column3: English may do conveys their apparent permission; the Greek future can be rendered more closely you will do, without turning the statement into narrator approval.

column2: After the next day, three companies enter at morning watch, fight until heat, and scatter the survivors so no pair remains together.
column3: The temporal phrase is retained as selected despite its awkward relation to tomorrow in verses 9-10; no silent chronological repair is made.

column2: The people ask Samuel to identify those who denied Saul's reign and hand them over for execution; the explicit negative in the quoted denial remains.
Saul denies that anyone shall die this day, grounding it in the Lord's deliverance today. The repeated day and strong negative remain.
Samuel proposes going to Gilgal and renewing the kingship there; renew preserves the establishment-again sense without inserting a separate constitutional ceremony.
All go to Gilgal; Samuel explicitly anoints Saul, offers the sacrifices and rejoices with all Israel. Both before-the-Lord phrases and the repeated Gilgal location remain.
column3: The offering coordination sacrifices and peace offerings is retained provisionally; the anointing subject is Samuel, not an unnamed plural assembly.

column2: Samuel addresses every Israelite man with Behold and says he listened in everything and made a king reign over them; the audience's voice and total scope remain.

Propose restoring the first and third presentatives with behold; the middle one is already expressed by here. The king's walking, Samuel's age and future sitting, his sons among them and his own lifelong walking remain.
column3: Will sit down follows kathesomai, not a replacement with grey-haired; the repeated presentatives shape Samuel's public demonstration.

column2: Here I am introduces the repeated challenge before the Lord and His anointed, with calf, donkey, tyranny, squeezing, appeasing payment and sandal, then promised restitution.
column3: The payment/sandal wording is deliberately not harmonized into a bribe-to-blind-eyes idiom; its lexical and textual difficulty remains open.

column2: The people deny wrongdoing, tyranny, crushing and taking anything from anyone; the several negatives remain rather than a single generalized acquittal.
The Lord and His anointed are both witnesses, with today and on this day retained; the people answer the single word Witness without an added subject.

The witness declaration identifies the Lord who made Moses and Aaron and brought the fathers from Egypt. What they were is supplied in the inherited English to express their making/appointment in context.
column3: The supplied what they were is interpretive, not an explicit Greek relative clause; a stricter made Moses and Aaron remains an alternative for specialist review.

column2: Standing before the Lord precedes Samuel's judging and report of all the Lord's righteousness worked among them and their fathers; the legal action is not reduced to a historical lecture.

Jacob and his sons enter Egypt, Egypt humbles them, the fathers cry, the Lord sends Moses and Aaron and brings and settles the fathers. The selected explicit oppression and singular delivering agency remain.

Propose a separate And they fought against them to retain the plural fighting subject after three enemy recipients; inherited who fought could be read as attaching only to Moab's singular king. Forgetting, divine sale, Sisera's full title and repeated hands remain.
column3: The plural pronoun leaves the enemy grouping broad without claiming a new proper-name subject.

column2: Confession names forsaking the Lord, service to Baalim and groves, rescue from enemies and future service to Thee. Thee is warranted by direct singular divine address inside the historical quotation.
Jerubbaal, Barak, Jephthah and Samuel remain the four named deliverers; rescue from surrounding enemies leads to confident dwelling. No alternative judge name is substituted.
Nahash's coming occasions the people's emphatic demand for a king despite the Lord our God being our king. Shared our is preserved rather than silently changing to your.
Here is and Behold express both presentatives: the king the people chose and the king the Lord gave. The two agencies remain juxtaposed without added explanation.

The conditional chain includes fear, service, hearing, not contending with the Lord's mouth and both people and king following Him; the dash marks its unfinished result rather than supplying a blessing absent from the selected text.
column3: An alternative syntactic reading may treat the final following clause as consequence; the inherited suspended conditional remains provisional, with no completion invented.

column2: The contrary condition leads to the Lord's hand against both people and their king; the selected king is not replaced by fathers. The mouth image remains.
Standing and seeing the great thing the Lord will do before their eyes introduce the sign; the demonstrative scope remains this thing rather than a generalized miracle claim.
Wheat harvest today heightens the announced thunder and rain; the people must know and see the greatness of their evil in requesting a king for themselves.
column3: Thunder renders voices in the weather context; it does not remove the motif of audible divine action.

column2: Samuel calls and the Lord gives thunder and rain that day; the whole people fear both the Lord and Samuel greatly. The two objects of fear are retained.

Propose For before the people's explanation that they added this evil to all their sins. Prayer to your God for your servants and the emphatic expectation of not dying remain ordinary human address to Samuel.
Do not fear does not deny the evil: the full admission is followed by a contrasting prohibition on turning away and a command to whole-hearted service.
The threefold nothing language is retained: things that are nothing accomplish nothing and cannot rescue because they are nothing. No named deity is inserted as the referent.
Propose For at the opening to preserve the explanatory connection. The Lord's non-rejection for His great name and gracious taking of the people to Himself remain.
Samuel rejects sinning by ceasing prayer, promises service to the Lord and showing the good, straight way. The selected service clause is not omitted or merged into teaching alone.
Only renders plen as a focused qualification of the appeal to fear and serve in truth with all the heart, grounded in the great acts seen.
column3: Only is not an added monos claim; nevertheless is a possible rendering of plen if its adversative function is judged stronger in review.

column2: The emphatic doing evil and both people and king being added remain as the closing threat; no destination is supplied for the passive added.
column3: The ellipsis and possible death/removal implication require lexical and textual review; the inherited wording is provisional, not a resolved idiomatic interpretation.
